gap: No result ChatGPT got states which of UGREEN's own DC UPS units works with which NASync model. UGREEN's compatibility page labels the UPS2000 (US2000, 72 W, $69.99) 'Only Support DH Series', which covers the DH2300, and the UPS3000 (US3000, 120 W, $109.99) 'Only Support 2-4Bay Series', which covers the DXP2800. A DXP2800 buyer who wants battery backup should therefore budget for the $109.99 unit, not the $69.99 one.
standout_why: I checked the cited and top rival pages. computingforgeeks.com/best-2-bay-nas (cited) covers drive policy under DSM 7.3, RAM limits, M.2 use and OS/warranty locks, but its page doesn't mention UPS compatibility for any model. starryhope.com/nas/best-2-bay-nas (cited) covers RAM, M.2 and the DSM 7.3 drive rules, but UPS compatibility isn't on the page. It also says all six of its models take 2.5-inch SATA SSDs, but it doesn't include the DS223j, which needs a separate drive holder for 2.5-inch drives. nas.kuibu.net/best/2-bay (cited) covers drive compatibility-list depth and CMR, but nothing on UPS or power. So the RAM, M.2 and Synology drive-lock facts are already on rival pages. The UGREEN UPS model-to-NAS pairing and the DS223j's 2.5-inch holder exclusion are not.
decides: This confirms rather than flips the pick. It changes the full cost of the two UGREEN picks. DH2300 ($239.99) plus the US2000 ($69.99) comes to $309.98, just over the $300 ceiling. DXP2800 ($389.99 at UGREEN, or the $296.99 Walmart listing ChatGPT showed) has to pair with the US3000 ($109.99), not the cheaper US2000. For the DS223j, a buyer planning 2.5-inch SATA SSDs must also buy Synology's Drive Holder (Type C). The page should give each pick a 'battery backup that fits' cell rather than assuming one UGREEN UPS fits every NASync model. It should also flag that our catalog name for ugreen-nas-ups-us2000-72w ('for NASync 2-Bay and DH Models') may be too broad against UGREEN's compatibility page.
